data.body: Fixes bugs B9f8019c521 and B1172da8c35. (1) merge's result and its worktree.merged event carry sha = the commit the base now points at (the merge commit; the branch head on a fast-forward), matching what the PR path already records (info.merge_sha); the branch's head moves to branch_head. complete without --sha reports the merge commit it records. (2) ddflow merge itself exits 0 when run from inside the item's worktree; the exit 1 + 'pwd: getcwd' is the CALLING shell's post-command pwd failing in the directory merge just deleted. Merge now keeps the worktree when the caller (CLI cwd, or called_from) stands in it, says so and where to cd, and that cleanup --apply removes it once complete.
data.title: merge reports the merge commit on the base as sha (branch head as branch_head), and keeps a worktree the caller stands in instead of deleting its shell's directory (fixes bug B9f8019c521, B1172da8c35)

evidence.note: R90b1cb89a9 CONFIRMED (scratch repo: merge printed ce4d4aa0 = branch head; main's merge commit befb7d5). R0695bb3008 CONFIRMED: ddflow merge from inside the tree exits 0 in plain bash; as the last command of a harness Bash call 'pwd: getcwd' + exit 1 -- the caller's post-command pwd in the deleted cwd, not ddflow's exit.

recall 'merge result sha worktree removal': no decision governs merge's sha; L-fix-activates-advice applied: the kept-tree remedy names 'ddflow cleanup --apply', which only removes merged, unheld trees (services/cleanup.py classification), safe to run once the item is complete. PR path already records the forge merge commit as sha (services/flow.py), so the local path now agrees.

ab90e22: api.merge reports sha = the base after the landing (landed_after), branch_head = the branch's head, in the result, the worktree.merged event and the merge gate evidence; complete without --sha reports the recorded merged_sha; the item's tree is kept (with 'cd <primary>' and cleanup remedy) when called_from or the CLI's own cwd is inside it (tree disposal extracted to _dispose_tree); CLI and MCP payloads add branch_head, worktree, worktree_removed. Consumers checked: fold merged_sha, progress commits, versions is-ancestor, ports (use landed range; cherry-pick fallback only for old events), _tree_let_go, reporting -- all correct with the landing commit.

env -u PYTHONPATH -u DDFLOW_AGENT uv run --with pytest-xdist pytest -q -n 48 on ab90e22: 2936 passed, 1 skipped in 101.7s. Regression: tests/test_merge_report.py 5/5 FAIL on the unfixed code (sha c98083..!= main 7b0a56..; human line names the branch head; complete --json sha ''; 'pwd: getcwd' exit 1 from 'ddflow merge T1 && pwd -P' in the tree; no worktree_removed key), 5/5 pass after. An earlier full run had 1 failure in tests/test_review_parallel.py::test_every_copy_off_contract_is_still_not_a_review that passes alone and on the rerun (unrelated file, load flake).

Walked each strategy: no-ff/ff (sha = base tip = merge commit or branch head on ff), squash (sha = the squash commit; the branch head is not on the base at all, so the old value was wrong there too), already-up-to-date (base tip, contains the work), throwaway-tree merge for an unchecked-out target (W.rev reads the moved ref). _stands_in: primary is never inside a linked tree; MCP called_from is the server's dir, so an MCP merge still removes the tree unless the server itself runs in it (then keeping is right too). complete: sha falls back to merged_sha only when --sha is omitted; fold already did the same. Consumers of merged_sha (versions is-ancestor, ports, _tree_let_go, progress commits) all hold for the landing commit; PR path already stored the merge commit.

No existing 'is the caller inside this tree' helper in api/lifecycle (callers_tree answers a different question: which item's tree the caller is in); _dispose_tree is the old inline block extracted (C901), not a copy. Payload tuple is declared in two places (CLI MERGE_PAYLOAD and the MCP spec) as before; both changed identically.
